land.text: Pisa and its countryside, 'annexation to the Republic of Florence' in 1406

successors.note: Pisa was a Visconti dominion from 13 February 1399 (sold by Gherardo Appiani to Gian Galeazzo Visconti), with Gabriele Maria Visconti as ruler 1402-1406 (infobox).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1000-1009: Cliopatria starts the Republic in 1010, the infobox says 'Established: c. 1000'. The 1010 shape (the contado round Pisa, 2,595 km2, with Elba) is taken back to c. 1000. The page gives no extent and no infobox area, so the area check could not be made. The page puts no precise date on the commune: Henry IV 'granted them the right to name their own consuls' (undated) and Gregory VII recognized the Pisan maritime laws in 1077.

2,595 km2 for 1010-1084 (12 cells: Pisa 6, Livorno 4, Elba 2 and edge cells). Right for 1010-1050; Corsica is added from 1051 ('Admiral Jacopo Ciurini conquered Corsica', 1051-1052; the page's control span is 'Corsica from 1050 to 1295'), see republic-of-pisa_1051. 'In 1060, Pisa engaged in its first battle against Genoa.' The islands 'Elba, Gorgona, Pianosa, Giglio and Giannutri' are on the page without years; only Elba is in Cliopatria's shape.

correction.text: the Pisan contado with Corsica, conquered by Jacopo Ciurini in 1051-1052

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1051-1084: Corsica. 'Admiral Jacopo Ciurini conquered Corsica, provoking more resentment from the Genoese' (1051-1052); 'Corsica from 1050 to 1295'. The Corsica page has a different story: the island 'transfer[red]... to the papacy in 1077' and 'The Pope yielded civic administration to Pisa in 1090'; the Pisa page adds 'In 1092, Pope Urban II awarded Pisa supremacy over Corsica and Sardinia'. Cliopatria shows Corsica from 1085. This keyframe follows the Pisa page; the 33 Corsican cells are Cliopatria's.

13,813 km2 for 1085-1187 (46 cells: the contado and all of Corsica). Cliopatria's year follows the Corsica page ('The Pope yielded civic administration to Pisa in 1090'; Urban II's grant of 1092 on the Pisa page); the island is Pisan by conquest from 1051 per the Pisa page, so the shape is right from 1085 and extended back by the 1051 keyframe. The Genoese settlement of Bonifacio (1195) is on neither page.

correction.text: the Pisan contado and Corsica, without Sardinia before 1207

keyframe_review.note: 24,076 km2 for 1188-1201: adds 32 Sardinian cells (the Judicate of Cagliari, 8.5-9.7 E, 39.0-40.1 N). The Pisa page has 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324' and the Judicate of Cagliari page runs to 1258 ('Established: 1020; Disestablished: 1258'), 'Pisan pressure grew over time' without a year. The 1016 expedition 'in alliance with Genoa' captured Sardinia from Mujahid but is no Pisan possession. The Sardinian cells are removed for 1188-1201 and appear from 1207 as dominion.

correction.text: the Pisan contado and Corsica, without Sardinia before 1207

keyframe_review.note: 22,879 km2 for 1202-1209: three Corsican cells at the south end (8.8-9.2 E, 41.5-41.6 N) are dropped; neither page opened mentions Bonifacio (unverified: page budget). Sardinia is removed for 1202-1206 as for 1188; 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324' begins in 1207 (see republic-of-pisa_1207).

union.text: the Pisan contado and Corsica, without Sardinia before 1207

correction.text: the contado and Corsica, with the Judicates of Cagliari and Gallura under Pisan dominion

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1207-1209: 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324' and 'the dominion over the giudicati of Cagliari and Gallura'. Both judicates remain states (Cagliari to 1258 per its page); their lands are drawn as Pisan dominion (vassal) from 1207. Cliopatria's Judicate of Gallura row ends 1209, its Cagliari row 1187.

27,574 km2 for 1210-1226 (89 cells: contado, Corsica 30, Sardinia 45). Cliopatria's Sardinian cells now include the Gallura country (40.3-41.2 N), which fits 'the dominion over the giudicati of Cagliari and Gallura'. The 45 Sardinian cells are Pisan dominion, not direct land, until 1258.
27,695 km2 for 1227-1259, one more Corsican cell (9.05 E, 41.6 N); no page opened explains it (unverified: page budget).

27,741 km2 for 1260-1394: Corsica (31 cells) and Sardinia (45) are kept to 1394 and then dropped in 1395. The pages put the ends much earlier: Corsica 'fell to Genoa in 1284, following the battle of Meloria' (Corsica page; the Pisa page says 'Corsica from 1050 to 1295'), and Sardinia ran 'from 1207 to 1324' (Pisa page). This shape holds for 1260-1283; see _1284 and _1324. From 1258 the Cagliari lands are Pisan direct possession (Cagliari page: 'in 1258 the history of the giudicato came to a sudden close', 'Pisa maintained the control over Castel di Castro'); two thirds of the judicate went to Arborea and Gallura, so the shape overstates the direct holding.

correction.text: the contado and Sardinia (Cagliari direct, Gallura under dominion), without Corsica

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1284-1323: Corsica lost. 'it fell to Genoa in 1284, following the battle of Meloria against Pisa' (Corsica page); the Pisa page has 'Corsica from 1050 to 1295' and, after Meloria, 'the renunciation of any claim on Corsica'. The Pisa page also has 'the sale of part of Sardinia to Genoa in 1299', without naming the part, so Sardinia stays whole here.

correction.text: the Pisan contado alone, after the loss of Sardinia

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1324-1394: Sardinia lost. 'In 1323 James II formed an alliance with Hugh II of Arborea' and 'occupied the Pisan territories of Cagliari and Gallura along with the city of Sassari'; 'Beginning in 1324, James and his successors conquered the island of Sardinia'; the Pisa page: 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324'. Cliopatria keeps both islands until 1394; its 1395 shape (the contado alone, 2,642 km2) is the right land from 1324.

2,642 km2 for 1395-1401, the contado alone (Pisa 6, Livorno 4, Elba 2). Right, with the islands gone since 1284 and 1324. The Pisa page: 'on February 13, 1399, the lord of Pisa Gherardo Appiani sold the city and the countryside' to Gian Galeazzo Visconti; the infobox gives Gabriele Maria Visconti as ruler 1402-1406. Cliopatria ends the Republic in 1401.

correction.text: the Pisan contado under Visconti rule

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1402-1405: Cliopatria ends the row in 1401, but the Pisa page has the city under Visconti rule (Gabriele Maria Visconti 1402-1406) until 'Annexed by the Republic of Florence: 1406'. The contado of 1395 is kept (the pages say nothing of its extent).

ledger.note: c. 1000: the commune of Pisa. Infobox 'Established: c. 1000'; Henry IV 'granted them the right to name their own consuls, advised by a Council of Elders' (undated). The page says nothing of the state it left.

ledger.counterpart: Corsica (local rulers; no state named on the page)
ledger.note: 1051-1052: Pisa takes Corsica. 'Admiral Jacopo Ciurini conquered Corsica, provoking more resentment from the Genoese'; the infobox control span is 'Corsica from 1050 to 1295'. The Corsica page says the island passed to the papacy in 1077 and that 'The Pope yielded civic administration to Pisa in 1090'; the Pisa page adds Urban II's supremacy grant of 1092.

June 1114: the Pisan-Catalan crusade reaches the Balearics. 'The combined Crusader fleet raided Ibiza in June' 1114, after the fleet that left Pisa in August 1113 was diverted by a storm; 'The Crusaders invested Palma de Majorca in August 1114.' The Pisa page: 'Pisan merchants were among the initiators of the 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition'. [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: year moved from 1113 to June 1114 and source changed to the expedition page; counterpart set to taifa-of-majorca.]

1115: the Balearics are lost. 'In April 1115 the city capitulated' (Palma), but 'The conquest of the Balearics lasted no more than a few months' and 'In 1115 they were reconquered by the Almoravids of peninsular Iberia' (the lead says 'only until the next year'). The Pisa page's infobox span 'Balearics from 1115 to 1184' is not a holding: the expedition page has no Pisan rule after 1115, and the almoravid-dynasty and taifa-of-majorca dossiers hold the islands from 1115. [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: end moved from 1184 to 1115, counterpart set to taifa-of-majorca (the occupied state; its dossier has the 1114-1115 contest with Pisa and the 1115 loss to the Almoravids), source changed to the expedition page.]
Cliopatria's shape drops three Corsican cells at the southern tip in 1202; neither the Corsica page nor the Pisa page mentions Bonifacio or any Genoese settlement. Page silent.

1207: the Judicate of Cagliari under Pisan dominion. 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324' and 'the dominion over the giudicati of Cagliari and Gallura'. The Cagliari page has 'Pisan pressure grew over time' and, in 1256, John trying 'to throw off the Pisan yoke'.

1207: the Judicate of Gallura under Pisan dominion. 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324' and 'the dominion over the giudicati of Cagliari and Gallura'. Cliopatria's Gallura row ends in 1209 and Pisa's shape takes the country in 1210.

1256: Cagliari rebels against Pisa. 'John tried to throw off the Pisan yoke' by allying with Genoa and was assassinated by Pisan agents; 'Pisa and the other Giudicati attacked Cagliari besieging Santa Igia' (the siege itself is undated).
1258: Santa Igia falls. 'In 1258 the history of the giudicato came to a sudden close.'

1258: the Pisan dominion over Cagliari becomes possession. 'in 1258 the history of the giudicato came to a sudden close' (infobox 'Disestablished: 1258'; succeeded by the Republic of Pisa and the Judicate of Arborea).

1258: Pisa takes the Judicate of Cagliari, except what goes to Arborea and Gallura. The judicate's 'territory was partitioned in three parts that were assigned to the Della Gherardesca family, Arborea and Gallura', and 'Pisa maintained the control over Castel di Castro'. The Pisan share is the Della Gherardesca part and the castle; Cliopatria's shape gives Pisa the whole judicate.

1282: the Corsican quarrel with Genoa. 'In 1282, Pisa tried to gain control of the commerce and administration of Corsica'; the war ends in the battle of 5-6 August 1284. The Pisa page: 'In 1060, Pisa engaged in its first battle against Genoa.'

1284: Corsica falls to Genoa. 'it fell to Genoa in 1284, following the battle of Meloria against Pisa.' The Pisa page dates the end of its control to 1295 ('Corsica from 1050 to 1295') and has Pisa renounce any claim on Corsica after Meloria.

5-6 August 1284: Genoa wins at Meloria. 'on 5 and 6 August 1284 between the fleets of the Republics of Genoa and Pisa'; 'The victory of Genoa and the destruction of the Pisan fleet marked the decline of the Republic of Pisa.' Two years later Genoa took Porto Pisano and filled up the harbour (undated).

region.text: the Pisan territories of Cagliari and Gallura

ledger.note: 1323: James II of Aragon invades Pisan Sardinia. 'In 1323 James II formed an alliance with Hugh II of Arborea' and 'occupied the Pisan territories of Cagliari and Gallura along with the city of Sassari'.

1324: Gallura leaves Pisan dominion. 'occupied the Pisan territories of Cagliari and Gallura' in 1323; 'Beginning in 1324, James and his successors conquered the island of Sardinia'; the Pisa page: 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324'.

1324: Sardinia is lost to Aragon. 'Beginning in 1324, James and his successors conquered the island of Sardinia'; the Pisa page gives 'Sardinia from 1207 to 1324' and 'from 1323, the Aragonese conquest of Sardinia began'. Neither page gives the date of the fall of Cagliari (Castel di Castro).
1324: the Aragonese conquest of Pisan Sardinia is made. 'Beginning in 1324, James and his successors conquered the island of Sardinia.'

13 February 1399: Pisa is sold to the Visconti. 'on February 13, 1399, the lord of Pisa Gherardo Appiani sold the city and the countryside' to Gian Galeazzo Visconti; Gabriele Maria Visconti is ruler 1402-1406 (infobox).
1406: Florence annexes Pisa. Infobox 'Annexed by the Republic of Florence: 1406'; Florence 'ordered the annexation to the Republic of Florence'. The Meloria page: 'Florence conquered Pisa in 1406'.

wars.name: Pisan wars with Genoa over Corsica
wars.outcome: Genoa won the battle of Meloria on 5-6 August 1284; Corsica 'fell to Genoa in 1284' (Corsica page); Pisa renounced any claim to it (Pisa page, which dates the end of its control to 1295). Genoa took Porto Pisano two years later.
wars.note: The Pisa page dates Pisa's first battle with Genoa to 1060 and calls the republic 'in perennial struggle with the Republic of Lucca, the Republic of Florence and Volterra' without years.

wars.name: Pisan war on the Judicate of Cagliari
wars.outcome: Santa Igia fell in 1258 and the judicate 'was partitioned in three parts that were assigned to the Della Gherardesca family, Arborea and Gallura', Pisa keeping Castel di Castro.
wars.note: Judge John allied with Genoa in 1256 and was assassinated by Pisan agents; the siege is undated on the page.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Pisan Sardinia
wars.outcome: James II and Hugh II of Arborea occupied the Pisan lands of Cagliari and Gallura and the city of Sassari in 1323; the conquest of the island begins in 1324 and ends Pisa's Sardinian control ('Sardinia from 1207 to 1324').
wars.note: The page does not mention the battle of Lucocisterna, Castel di Castro or a treaty of 1326; the fall of Castel di Castro is therefore undated here.

wars.name: Florentine annexation of Pisa
wars.outcome: Pisa, a Visconti dominion since 1399, was annexed by Florence in 1406; Cliopatria ends the Republic in 1401.
wars.note: The pages opened give no siege or capitulation date.

wars.name: Balearic expedition
wars.outcome: 'Pisan merchants were among the initiators of the 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition'; the infobox control span reads 'Balearics from 1115 to 1184'.
wars.note: The page gives no result beyond the control span. [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: the occupation ends in 1115, not 1184; see the ledger.]

certainty.note: The contado's land frontier with Lucca, Florence and Volterra ('perennial struggle', no years or lines on the page) was never surveyed; the island coasts of Corsica and Sardinia are natural limits but Pisan control of both was dominion, not a drawn border.

sources.title: Republic of Pisa
sources.note: Infobox (Capital: Pisa; Established c. 1000; Annexed by Florence 1406); Corsica 1050-1295 (Ciurini 1051-52, Urban II 1092); Sardinia 1207-1324; Balearics 1115-1184; the sale of Pisa to Visconti on 13 February 1399. No area.

sources.title: Battle of Meloria (1284)
sources.note: 5-6 August 1284; 1282 Corsican quarrel; Porto Pisano two years later. Silent on when Corsica was lost, on 1288 and on any 1299 treaty.

sources.title: History of Corsica
sources.note: Papal transfer 1077, civic administration to Pisa 1090, Corsica falls to Genoa in 1284. Silent on 1133, Bonifacio and 1299.

sources.title: Judicate of Cagliari
sources.note: Pisan pressure; John's revolt in 1256; the judicate ends in 1258 and is partitioned between the Della Gherardesca, Arborea and Gallura; Pisa keeps Castel di Castro. Silent on 1015-16 and on Pisan rule after 1258.

sources.title: Kingdom of Sardinia (1324-1720)
sources.note: 1297 grant of the Regnum Sardiniae et Corsicae; the 1323 Aragonese advance on the Pisan territories of Cagliari and Gallura and Sassari; conquest from 1324. Silent on Lucocisterna, Castel di Castro and a 1326 treaty.

sources.title: 1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition
sources.note: Added by reviewer eu-13-h: fleet left Pisa August 1113, Ibiza raided June 1114, Palma invested August 1114 and capitulated April 1115; 'The conquest of the Balearics lasted no more than a few months'; Almoravid reconquest 1115.

notes: Cliopatria's Republic of Pisa row (1010-1401) is kept as the base: the contado of 12 cells, Corsica from 1085 and Sardinia from 1188. The pages put each island on a different clock: Corsica from 1051 (Pisa page; Corsica page has the papal transfer of 1077 and Pisan administration from 1090; Cliopatria 1085) to 1284 (Corsica page; Pisa page 1295; Cliopatria 1394); Sardinia from 1207 (Pisa page; the Judicate of Cagliari lasted to 1258 and Gallura's row ends 1209) to 1324 (Pisa page and Kingdom of Sardinia page; Cliopatria 1394). Cliopatria's 1395 shape (the contado alone) is therefore right from 1324, not 1395. The state ends in 1406 with the Florentine annexation, not in 1401; it was a Visconti dominion from 13 February 1399. The Sardinian lands are dominion (vassal) from 1207 and possession from 1258 only for the Cagliari lands (the Pisa page: 'dominion over the giudicati of Cagliari and Gallura'); the Cagliari page makes the Della Gherardesca family (Pisan) one of three heirs, so Cliopatria's whole-judicate shape overstates the direct holding. Cross-check for the Arborea dossier: it has the fall of Castel di Castro in June 1326; the pages opened here end the Pisan Sardinia in 1324. Gallura: the giudicato-of-gallura dossier has Gallura passing to Pisa in 1287; no page opened here says so, and the vassal event runs 1207 to 1324. Not settled: the sale of part of Sardinia to Genoa in 1299 (Pisa page, no place named); the islands Elba, Gorgona, Pianosa, Giglio and Giannutri (listed without years; only Elba is in Cliopatria's shape); the Balearic span 1115-1184 (infobox control span, possibly a trading presence); the wars with Lucca, Florence and Volterra (no years); the third Corsican quarrel; Ugolino della Gherardesca; Porto Pisano's destruction (about 1286, undated); the Genoese Bonifacio of 1195 (the 1202 corner is a Cliopatria change the pages do not explain). No page gives an area, so the area comparison could not be made; Cliopatria's 27,741 km2 for 1260-1394 is unchecked. No ruler strip: the infobox lists only Gabriele Maria Visconti (1402-1406). The predecessor (the March of Tuscany, duchy-of-tuscia in group eu-13) is not on the page opened, so predecessors is empty. Counterparts without a dossier: Corsica's local rulers before 1051; the Balearic holders. Gazetteer names: none missing (Corsica, Sardinia and the Balearic Islands are regions). [Reviewer eu-13-h, 2026-10-25: the Balearic occupation now runs June 1114 to 1115 (1113-1115 Balearic Islands expedition page: the conquest lasted no more than a few months; Almoravid reconquest 1115); the infobox span 1115-1184 is not drawn.]
